reason: Core method exploits ADR cross-market pricing discrepancies with 50% discretionary judgment on multiple live factors (S&P, commodities, volume) and overnight timing risk; no concrete long-only daily-bar rules extractable.

universe.description: dual-listed ADRs (e.g. BHP, PLS) trading in Australia + US/Europe

setup.rule: US ADR trades at discount/premium to Australia primary
setup.quote: if Australia is up 10% versus the US, I might not try to fade it... if the US is up 10% on low volume versus Australia, there is a... massive discrepancies

entry.rule: Buy US side at 1-5% discount after checking S&P, copper, iron ore, Rio London; widen band on mixed signals
entry.quote: I'll most likely be buying it... BHP should be up 0 to 2% tomorrow. So I won't buy if it's flat, but I'll buy at maybe a 1 or maybe even 2% discount

exits.rule: Sell ASAP next day in Australia (convert or DMA)
exits.quote: often I found it's best if I just try to sell it ASAP the next day. Sell it in Australia

sizing.rule: Scale exponentially larger on A+ setups; often 50-70% of foreign volume
sizing.quote: when you have an A+ trade, you should do exponentially more size... in the PLS example, I think I was like 60, 70% of the volume

market_filter.rule: Check S&P move, sector peers, no negative news before committing size
market_filter.quote: checked everywhere, checked Bloomberg, Reuters, Twitter... No news. And meanwhile, the ES was still rallying

ambiguities.issue: No explicit numeric thresholds or daily-bar signals given
ambiguities.assumption: Method cannot be approximated on daily US bars
